name: Krippenmuseum Stamserhaus Wenns
kurzbeschreibung: The Nativity Museum in the historic Stamserhaus in Wenns: the oldest farmhouse in the Pitztal valley (15th century) with over 40 valuable Tyrolean Christmas cribs.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historically significant Krippenmuseum Stamserhaus (Nativity Museum Stamserhaus) is located in the traffic-calmed village center of Wenns in the front Pitztal valley (Imst district) at an altitude of around 980 meters. Framed by the picturesque Pitztal mountain landscape, the museum is housed in the so-called Stamserhaus – the oldest preserved farmhouse in the entire Pitztal valley, whose foundations and ridge beams date back dendrochronologically to 1520. As a renowned cultural site of supra-regional importance, the house preserves the rich heritage of the Wenns Nativity Association, the oldest Nativity scene building association in the world (founded in 1860).

Route & Requirements

The building itself is an outstanding architectural monument: originally built as a monastic farmstead of the famous Cistercian Abbey of Stams, the property boasts Gothic walls, artfully paneled Swiss pine parlors, historic smoke kitchens, and ancient beamed ceilings. In the atmospherically lit rooms, the museum presents over 40 valuable original Nativity scenes from five centuries. Wenns is considered the cradle of the Tyrolean Nativity tradition, which is officially recognized by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage. Among the most precious exhibits are historical box cribs from the 18th and 19th centuries with hand-carved figures by renowned masters such as Josef Georg Witwer or the sculptor family Schuler.

Visit & Arrival

The Nativity Museum in the Stamserhaus is open to visitors during the winter season (end of November to end of February) and the summer season (July to September) on Fridays from 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM (special guided tours for groups, clubs, and school classes of 6 or more people are possible year-round by prior arrangement). Admission prices (as of season 2025/2026): Adults approx. €5.00, seniors approx. €4.00, children and teenagers (6 to 15 years) approx. €2.50, toddlers free; family ticket approx. €12.00. Holders of the regional Pitztal Summer Card enjoy free admission! Arrival by car: Via the Inntalautobahn A12 (Imst/Pitztal exit), then continue on the Pitztaler Landesstraße L16 for about eight kilometers to Wenns. Parking is available in the village center at the municipal office (free). By public transport: ÖBB to Imst-Pitztal train station, from there VVT bus line 4204 runs every half hour directly to the Wenns Gemeindeamt stop (only a two-minute walk).

Tips

The ground floor of the museum is barrier-free via a ramp; a traditional wooden staircase leads to the historic parlors on the first floor. Take your time to admire the hand-painted Nativity backgrounds, which show detailed vedutas of historic Tyrolean villages. Combine your museum visit with a walk along the sunny Wennser Besinnungsweg or a stop at one of the traditional inns in the village square.
